reversibility_triggers.decision: publish to PyPI as `amazing-gmail-mcp` (`gmail-mcp` is taken); import package `gmail_mcp`, tool prefix `gmail_`
reversibility_triggers.trigger: the user registers the trusted publisher under a different free name
reversibility_triggers.fallback: rename dist + console scripts in lockstep on main before the first release; import package and tool prefix never change

reversibility_triggers.decision: v0.1 requests ONLY gmail.readonly: no scope that can send (gmail.compose and gmail.modify both send; research/2026-11-10-gmail-mcp/00-sintesis.md)
reversibility_triggers.trigger: the user wants drafts or label changes
reversibility_triggers.fallback: a second, separately named entry per company with its own refresh token and compose/modify scope, behind GMAIL_ALLOW_WRITES; the read-only entry stays as is

reversibility_triggers.decision: one server entry per company, refresh token from env (1Password), account pinned at startup with users.getProfile == GMAIL_ACCOUNT
reversibility_triggers.trigger: a mailbox needs domain-wide delegation (service account) instead of a user grant
reversibility_triggers.fallback: an alternative credential source in auth.py behind an explicit env var; the account pin stays mandatory

reversibility_triggers.decision: project scope = GMAIL_SCOPE_LABEL (labelIds[]) and/or GMAIL_SCOPE_QUERY (parenthesized, unbalanced user queries refused), re-checked after every fetch by id; a filter, not a security boundary
reversibility_triggers.trigger: a project needs a boundary the agent cannot leave
reversibility_triggers.fallback: a separate Google account or delegated mailbox for that project; never more parsing in the scope module
